## Project Overview

This portfolio demonstrates practical R programming skills in data management, quality assurance, and longitudinal health data analysis.
Using an educational hypertension study data set, the project illustrates a reproducible analytical workflow, including data import, validation, duplicate detection, data integration, variable derivation, descriptive analysis, and visualization.
The analysis focuses on changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP) across study visits and differences between intervention and usual care groups.

## Analytical Workflow

1. Data Import and Validation
2. Data Quality Assessment
3. Duplicate Detection and Data Integration
4. Longitudinal Data Transformation
5. Variable Derivation and Missing Data Handling
6. Descriptive Analysis and Data Visualization
7. Reproducibility and Quality Assurance Checks


```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
```


```{r}
# Check available data files
list.files(here::here("data"))

# Verify that all required files exist
required_files <- c(
  "edu_htn_subjects.csv",
  "edu_htn_visits.csv",
  "edu_htn_analysis.csv",
  "edu_htn_adherence.csv"
)

stopifnot(
  all(file.exists(here::here("data", required_files)))
)

cat("All required data files found.\n")
```

## 1. Data Import and Validation
This section imports subject-level and visit-level data with explicitly defined variable types to ensure consistency and prevent data parsing errors.
```{r}

subjects <- read_csv(
  here("data", "edu_htn_subjects.csv"),
  col_types = cols(
    subject_id = col_character(),
    arm = col_character(),
    site = col_character(),
    age = col_double(),
    sex = col_character(),
    race = col_character(),
    bmi = col_double(),
    sbp_base = col_double(),
    randomized = col_character(),
    randomization_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    first_dose_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    .default = col_guess()
  )
)

visits <- read_csv(
  here("data", "edu_htn_visits.csv"),
  col_types = cols(
    subject_id = col_character(),
    visit_code = col_character(),
    visit_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    sbp = col_double(),
    week = col_double()
  )
)

# Verify successful imports
cat("Subjects:", nrow(subjects), "rows\n")
cat("Visits:", nrow(visits), "rows\n")

# Check for parsing errors
stopifnot(
  nrow(problems(subjects)) == 0,
  nrow(problems(visits)) == 0
)

cat("Data imported successfully with no parsing errors.\n")
```
## 2. Data Quality Assessment
This section evaluates missing data and checks the completeness of subject-level and visit-level datasets before data integration and analysis.
```{r}
# Summarize missing values in subject-level data
missing_subjects <- subjects |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "n_missing"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing))

# Summarize missing values in visit-level data
missing_visits <- visits |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "n_missing"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing))

# Display results
print(missing_subjects)
print(missing_visits)

```
### Duplicate Detection and Key Integrity

```{r}
# Check duplicate subject IDs
duplicate_subjects <- subjects |>
  count(subject_id) |>
  filter(n > 1)

# Check duplicate subject-visit combinations
duplicate_visits <- visits |>
  count(subject_id, visit_code) |>
  filter(n > 1)

# Identify visit records without a matching subject
orphan_visits <- anti_join(
  visits,
  subjects,
  by = "subject_id"
)

# Summarize quality checks
cat("Duplicate subject IDs:", nrow(duplicate_subjects), "\n")
cat("Duplicate subject-visit pairs:", nrow(duplicate_visits), "\n")
cat("Orphan visit records:", nrow(orphan_visits), "\n")

# Validate data integrity
stopifnot(
  nrow(duplicate_subjects) == 0,
  nrow(duplicate_visits) == 0,
  nrow(orphan_visits) == 0
)

cat("All key integrity checks passed.\n")
```

## 3. Data Integration
Subject-level demographic information is merged with visit-level blood pressure measurements using a many-to-one relationship. Key integrity and row counts are verified to prevent unintended duplication or loss of records.
```{r}

# Merge visit-level data with subject-level characteristics
visit_plus <- visits |>
  left_join(
    subjects |>
      select(subject_id, arm, age, sex, site),
    by = "subject_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )

# Verify that the join preserved all visit records
stopifnot(
  nrow(visit_plus) == nrow(visits),
  sum(is.na(visit_plus$arm)) == 0,
  sum(is.na(visit_plus$age)) == 0
)

# Display dimensions of merged dataset
cat("Merged dataset:", nrow(visit_plus), "rows,",
    ncol(visit_plus), "columns\n")

cat("Data integration completed successfully.\n")

# Preview merged dataset
head(visit_plus)
```

## 4. Longitudinal Data Transformation
Visit-level blood pressure measurements are reshaped from long to wide format to support participant-level longitudinal analysis. Each participant has one row, with separate columns for systolic blood pressure measurements at each study visit.
```{r}

# Reshape longitudinal SBP measurements into wide format
sbp_wide <- visits |>
  select(subject_id, visit_code, sbp) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = visit_code,
    values_from = sbp,
    names_prefix = "sbp_"
  )

# Verify that each participant has one row
stopifnot(
  nrow(sbp_wide) == nrow(subjects),
  n_distinct(sbp_wide$subject_id) == nrow(sbp_wide)
)

# Display the reshaped dataset
cat("Wide dataset:", nrow(sbp_wide), "rows,",
    ncol(sbp_wide), "columns\n")

head(sbp_wide)
```

## 5. Variable Derivation and Missing Data Handling
Changes in systolic blood pressure are calculated relative to the baseline visit. A participant is classified as a responder if their Week 12 SBP decreased by at least 10 mmHg. Missing outcome values are preserved rather than treated as non-response.
```{r}

# Derive changes from baseline at each follow-up visit
sbp_derived <- sbp_wide |>
  mutate(
    chg_wk4  = sbp_WEEK4  - sbp_BASELINE,
    chg_wk8  = sbp_WEEK8  - sbp_BASELINE,
    chg_wk12 = sbp_WEEK12 - sbp_BASELINE
  )

# Classify Week 12 responders
sbp_derived <- sbp_derived |>
  mutate(
    responder = case_when(
      is.na(chg_wk12) ~ NA,
      chg_wk12 <= -10 ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

# Verify change calculations and missing value handling
stopifnot(
  sum(!is.na(sbp_derived$chg_wk12)) == 215,
  sum(is.na(sbp_derived$responder)) ==
    sum(is.na(sbp_derived$chg_wk12))
)

# Summarize derived variables
cat("Participants with observed Week 12 change:",
    sum(!is.na(sbp_derived$chg_wk12)), "\n")

cat("Participants with missing Week 12 change:",
    sum(is.na(sbp_derived$chg_wk12)), "\n")

cat("Week 12 responders:",
    sum(sbp_derived$responder, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

head(sbp_derived)
```

## 6. Descriptive Analysis and Data Visualization
Descriptive statistics are calculated to compare changes in systolic blood pressure and response rates between intervention and usual care groups. Participants with missing Week 12 outcomes are excluded from outcome-specific calculations but retained in the dataset.
```{r}

# Add treatment group information to derived dataset
analysis_data <- sbp_derived |>
  left_join(
    subjects |> select(subject_id, arm),
    by = "subject_id",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

# Confirm all subjects are retained
stopifnot(
  nrow(analysis_data) == nrow(subjects),
  sum(is.na(analysis_data$arm)) == 0
)

# Summarize Week 12 outcomes by treatment group
arm_summary <- analysis_data |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_observed = sum(!is.na(chg_wk12)),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(chg_wk12)),
    mean_change = round(mean(chg_wk12, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd_change = round(sd(chg_wk12, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    n_responders = sum(responder, na.rm = TRUE),
    responder_rate = round(
      100 * mean(responder, na.rm = TRUE), 1
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(arm_summary)
```
```{r}

# Visualize Week 12 SBP changes by treatment group
ggplot(
  analysis_data |> filter(!is.na(chg_wk12)),
  aes(x = arm, y = chg_wk12, fill = arm)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.7,
    outlier.shape = 16
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray40"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Systolic Blood Pressure at Week 12",
    subtitle = "Intervention vs. Usual Care",
    x = "Treatment Group",
    y = "Change in SBP from Baseline (mmHg)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Results Interpretation

### Results Interpretation
Among participants with observed Week 12 outcomes, the intervention group showed a greater mean reduction in systolic blood pressure (SBP) than the usual care group (-8.21 vs. -2.31 mmHg).
The responder rate was also higher in the intervention group (36.1%) compared with the usual care group (7.5%). A responder was defined as a participant whose SBP decreased by at least 10 mmHg from baseline.
The boxplot illustrates a downward shift in SBP changes among intervention participants relative to usual care participants.
These findings are descriptive and do not establish statistical significance or causal effects. Participants with missing Week 12 outcomes were excluded from outcome-specific summaries, which may introduce bias if missingness is related to treatment response.

## 7. Reproducibility and Quality Assurance Checks
Final assertions verify the integrity of the analytical dataset, consistency of derived variables, and preservation of missing outcome values.

```{r}

# Verify the analytical dataset
stopifnot(
  nrow(analysis_data) == 240,
  n_distinct(analysis_data$subject_id) == 240,
  sum(is.na(analysis_data$chg_wk12)) == 25,
  sum(analysis_data$responder, na.rm = TRUE) == 47,
  sum(arm_summary$n_total) == 240,
  sum(arm_summary$n_observed) == 215,
  sum(arm_summary$n_missing) == 25
)

# Verify the responder classification
stopifnot(
  all(
    analysis_data$responder[!is.na(analysis_data$chg_wk12)] ==
      (analysis_data$chg_wk12[!is.na(analysis_data$chg_wk12)] <= -10)
  )
)

cat("All final quality assurance checks passed.\n")

# Record the R environment for reproducibility
sessionInfo()
```
